mechanism_narrative: Transit mobility has improved for four consecutive weeks (-39.1 to -14.0), reflecting sustained return of commuting and errand trips. This steady transit recovery is a leading indicator that drives continued growth in retail-and-recreation footfall over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -39.1 to -14.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: Reject if TRANSIT continues improving but RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is not higher than its prior-28-day mean, or if TRANSIT reverses for two straight weeks while RETAIL_REC still rises.

mechanism_narrative: Residential time has slowly declined each week (3.3 to 2.6), indicating households are reducing time spent at home. If this decline crosses a lower threshold, it signals a behavioral shift toward more out-of-home discretionary activity, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 2.0 percentage points from its current 2.6 level
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 3.3 to 2.6 across four weeks
failure_condition: Reject if RESIDENTIAL crosses below 2.0 but RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean fails to exceed its prior-28-day mean, or if RESIDENTIAL stalls above 2.5 while RETAIL_REC still rises.

mechanism_narrative: Workplace mobility has plateaued near -29 for two weeks while TRANSIT continues to improve, implying the marginal transit gains reflect non-commute, leisure-oriented trips. This divergence between stabilized work travel and rising transit use is predicted to translate into higher retail-and-recreation visits.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES flat at -29.3/-29.0 while TRANSIT improved -18.9 to -14.0
failure_condition: Reject if WORKPLACES remains flat and TRANSIT keeps improving yet RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean does not exceed its prior-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under an easing state-of-emergency regime, early-recovery categories (GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS) surged sharply then plateaued or dipped in the latest week, indicating a saturation point in the first wave of policy-driven mobility recovery that typically precedes a stall in slower-to-recover retail activity.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM 7.4->6.9 and PARKS 16.3->11.9 both declined week-on-week after sharp earlier gains
regime_hint: state of emergency easing - restrictions phased down
failure_condition: Reject if GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS both plateau/decline but RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean rises above its prior-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility peaked at 16.3 and has since fallen to 11.9, consistent with seasonal cooling as Tokyo transitions into autumn, reducing outdoor leisure activity. This seasonal decline in outdoor recreation is expected to spill over into lower overall retail-and-recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from 16.3 to 11.9 in the most recent week
failure_condition: Reject if PARKS continues its decline but RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is higher than its prior-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The week-on-week improvement in TRANSIT sharply decelerated from +12.2 points to +4.9 points, signaling that the pace of policy-driven mobility recovery is slowing. This deceleration in a leading recovery indicator is predicted to translate into a flat or declining RETAIL_REC over the following week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week improvement falls below 5 points after exceeding 8 points the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT weekly improvement dropped from +12.2 to +4.9
failure_condition: Reject if TRANSIT's weekly gain stays below 5 points yet RETAIL_REC posts a gain of more than 5 points over the next week.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC itself has nearly flattened over the last two weeks (-16.7 then -17.9), suggesting consumer behavior has reached a short-term equilibrium after rapid recovery. This momentum stabilization implies RETAIL_REC will remain flat-to-slightly-lower rather than resume rapid growth in the immediate next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC moved from -16.7 to -17.9 week-on-week, nearly flat after prior rapid recovery
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC's next week mean rises by more than 5 points relative to the current flat plateau.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS have both plateaued or slightly declined after sharp recovery, while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated relative to baseline, jointly indicating that overall non-work mobility recovery is stalling across categories. This combined consolidation predicts that RETAIL_REC will also fail to grow and may dip over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS both declined week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL stayed above 2.5
failure_condition: Reject if GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS remain flat/declining and RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, yet RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean exceeds its prior-28-day mean by more than 5 points.
